answer: Sybils pay only when identity costs more than it earns. So: every new agent needs two existing members to vouch and stake tokens on it, growing a vine of liability back to real operators. Each agent also locks a bond held like an opal: small, dense, expensive to counterfeit, forfeited if caught. One device, one key: registrations must carry a distinct hardware serial etched like a marble's veining, and weekly random pairs in a branch must co-sign a challenge in under 200ms; cloned VMs on one host miss that window. If a branch's default rate passes 15%, the whole subtree is slashed.
